review.summary: The statements are in good shape. I found no theorem whose statement is weaker than its doc says in a way that misleads about the main results. Arith.lean and Fixup.lean (barely changed since the 2026-11-15 audit) are clean. In Heap.lean, every refinement theorem (rotateAt_refines_*, attachTo/substituteWith/switchWith_refines, insertFixupLoop_refines, insertFixup_refines(_depth)) states what its doc claims, and the hypotheses I examined there are all needed. The defects are in the per-address `_apply`/`_frame` lemmas: three hypotheses are provably unnecessary (tested by deleting them in a scratch file, see F1–F3). There are also a few doc sentences that disagree with the statement or the built code.

findings.title: switchWith_frame's hypothesis `h₀ : this ≠ node` is not needed
findings.description: `theorem switchWith_frame (h : Heap) (this node : Addr) (h₀ : this ≠ node) {x : Addr} (h₁ : x ≠ this) (h₂ : x ≠ childAt h node .left) (h₃ : x ≠ childAt h node .right) (h₄ : x ≠ parent h node)`. Its doc says only "`switchWith` touches four addresses: `this`, `node`'s two children and `node`'s parent", which holds on every heap. The write set does not depend on `this ≠ node`: the two reads made after a write (`parent h node`, `red h node`) read fields that the earlier writes to `this` never change. The proof uses `Ne.symm h₀` in its closing `simp`, so the unused-variable linter cannot flag it. CONVENTIONS.md ("Every hypothesis must be needed") requires dropping it.
findings.evidence: In the scratch file audit/t1.lean I restated the theorem without h₀ and proved it with the original `simp only [...] at h₂ h₃ h₄ ⊢`, then `by_cases h₀ : node = this; · subst h₀; simp [h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄]; · simp [h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄, h₀]`. It checks with `lake env lean` and no errors. Heap.lean has no callers of switchWith_frame, so nothing downstream breaks.
findings.fix:
Drop `h₀` and replace the proof's last line with the case split:
```lean
theorem switchWith_frame (h : Heap) (this node : Addr) {x : Addr}
    (h₁ : x ≠ this) (h₂ : x ≠ childAt h node .left) (h₃ : x ≠ childAt h node .right)
    (h₄ : x ≠ parent h node) : switchWith h this node x = h x := by
  simp only [switchWith, setChild_eq, setParentPtr, setParentSide, setColour, Heap.modify,
    childAt, parent, parentSide, red] at h₂ h₃ h₄ ⊢
  by_cases h₀ : node = this
  · subst h₀; simp [h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄]
  · simp [h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄, h₀]
```

findings.title: rotateAt_apply's `h₂ : this ≠ m` is not needed, and its doc's distinctness list is too strict
findings.description: The doc (lines 985-991) says: "`top` ... `m` ... and `P` ..., all distinct except that `m` and `P` may coincide". The statement correspondingly takes `(h₂ : this ≠ childAt h (childAt h this s.other) s)`, i.e. `this ≠ m`. That hypothesis is unnecessary. When `this = m`, the later writes `setParentPtr this top` and `setParentSide this s` overwrite the `parent` word that the `m` writes set. `this`'s `s.other` link then holds `m` (= `this`), which is exactly what the first branch of the `if` chain states. The `m` branch is shadowed by the `x = this` branch, so the stated result is unchanged. The statement is weaker than it could be, and the doc's "all distinct except" reflects the extra hypothesis rather than a real requirement.
findings.evidence: In the scratch file audit/t1.lean I restated the theorem without h₂. I kept the original proof except for the `x = this` case, which became `by_cases e : x = m; · subst e; simp [h₁, h₄]; · simp [h₁, h₄, e]`. It checks, with only an unused-simp-arg warning.
findings.fix: Drop `h₂` and use that case split in the `e₁` branch. In `rotateAt_refines_left`/`_right` (lines 1066, 1193), remove the corresponding argument from the `rotateAt_apply` calls. Reword the doc to "distinct except that `m` may coincide with `P` (a rotation at the root whose moving subtree is empty) or with `this`". Alternatively, list exactly the four disequalities the statement takes.

findings.title: switchWith_apply's `h₁ : this ≠ node` is not needed
findings.description: `theorem switchWith_apply (h : Heap) (this node : Addr) (h₁ : this ≠ node) (h₂ ...) ... (h₇ ...)`. Given h₂–h₇, the case `this = node` already satisfies the stated `if` chain. `this`'s record ends as `{h this with left := L, right := R, parent := P, side := ps, red := red h node}`, the first branch. So h₁ is redundant. It is the Rust's `debug_assert!(this != node)`, which the module doc lists as not modelled. Keeping it as a hypothesis is not dishonest, but CONVENTIONS.md asks for every hypothesis to be needed.
findings.evidence: In the scratch file audit/t2.lean, `switchWith_apply'` without h₁ checks: `by_cases h₁ : this = node`, then the original proof body after `subst` (with `hn1` removed) in the first case, and the original theorem in the second.
findings.fix: Either drop h₁ (wrap the proof in `by_cases h₁ : this = node`, as in the scratch file), or keep it and say in the doc that it is the `debug_assert!(this != node)` precondition kept for readability. The current wording ("`this` takes `node`'s children, slot and colour") does not justify it. Callers pass `htn` and are unaffected either way.

findings.title: rotateAt_parent_fields' doc reads as unconditional, but the statement takes two hypotheses
findings.description: The doc says: "Of `this`'s parent, `rotateAt` writes only the child link `this` hung from, which now holds `top`: the other link and the colour are kept, and so is the `parent` word unless ...". The statement assumes `(h₁ : parent h this ≠ this) (h₂ : parent h this ≠ childAt h this s.other)`, and h₂ is genuinely needed: if `P = top` and `parentSide h this = s`, the later write `setChild top s this` overwrites the link. The doc names the one exception it handles inside the conclusion (P = m) but not these two preconditions. Read alone, it claims the result for every heap.
findings.evidence: Reading the statement against `rotateAt`'s write order (lines 233-247): `setChild thisParent ps top` is followed by `setChild top s this`. With `thisParent = top` and `ps = s`, the slot ends holding `this`, not `top`.
findings.fix: Add to the doc: "for a parent distinct from `this` and from `top` (which `Located` guarantees: the slot's node is outside the subtree)".

findings.title: `Rep.root_fields` (and `substituteWith_refines_core`) take a membership witness where they mean "non-empty"
findings.description: `theorem root_fields (hr : Rep h head a p s t) {x : Addr} (hx : x ∈ t.toList)` uses `x` only to rule out `t = nil`. Every caller supplies it as `hr.root_mem hn` from `a ≠ head` (for example `insertFixup_refines` line 2189: `(hl.1.root_fields (hl.1.root_mem hn)).1`). `substituteWith_refines_core` likewise takes `(hthis : this ∈ t.toList)` to mean `this ≠ head`. The statements are honest but indirect: a reader must work out that an arbitrary `x` serves only as a non-emptiness witness.
findings.evidence: Read the proofs (`cases hr with | nil => simp at hx | node ... => ...`). `hx` is used only in the `nil` case.
findings.fix: State `root_fields (hr : Rep h head a p s t) (ha : a ≠ head)`, proved with `cases hr with | nil => exact absurd rfl ha | node _ _ hp hs => exact ⟨hp, hs⟩`, and let callers pass `hn` directly. Optionally take `this ≠ head` in `substituteWith_refines_core` too.

recommendations: insertFixup_refines_depth's doc (Heap.lean lines 2210-2212) says fuel at least the depth "always suffices". It suffices under the theorem's other hypotheses (a located real node, black root). Consider "suffices, under `insertFixup_refines`' other hypotheses".

rootColour_up_left's doc (line 1867), "A black (or absent) root stays so one step down the path", describes the hole moving up a step, from `.left c pp y b` to `pp`. "when the hole climbs one step" reads more accurately.

Heap.lean module doc line 21: "from any located subtree whose tree has a black root". The theorem also needs the subtree non-empty (`cur ≠ head`) and the fuel bound. Consider "from any located node, in a tree with a black root, given enough fuel".

Scratch files: scratch/t1.lean (F1, F2) and scratch/t2.lean (F3; its second lemma `rpf`, an attempt to drop h₂ from rotateAt_parent_fields, failed with a recursion-depth error, consistent with F4's analysis that h₂ is needed).

verdicts.reasoning: Verified in my own scratch file scratch/v1.lean. switchWith_frame' with no h₀ checks under `lake env lean` with no errors, using the proposed case split. grep finds no callers of switchWith_frame anywhere in Lean/. CONVENTIONS.md line 133 says "Every hypothesis must be needed", so the hypothesis should go. I lower the severity to low: the extra hypothesis only weakens a frame lemma nobody uses. It does not mislead about what is proven, and the Rust's debug_assert!(this != node) guarantees it anyway.

rotateAt_apply' without h₂ (this ≠ m) checks in v1.lean, with the e₁ branch split on `x = m`. The reason is the write order in rotateAt (Heap.lean lines 195-203). When this = m, the final setParentPtr this top / setParentSide this s overwrite the m writes, and this's o-link holds topSChild = this, which matches the first if-branch. The only callers are lines 1066 and 1193, which pass h₂ positionally. They need their second explicit argument removed. The doc at lines 985-991 does say "all distinct except that m and P may coincide", which is stricter than needed. m = this is a cycle that never occurs in a valid tree, so the fix's doc wording should say so or simply list the four disequalities.

switchWith_apply' without h₁ checks in v1.lean. With this = node, `subst`, then the original body (with hn1 removed) closes the goal, and the other case reuses the original theorem. The hypothesis is redundant given h₂–h₇. It does model a debug_assert precondition that the def's doc already lists as not modelled. Either fix the reviewer proposes is acceptable. Dropping it is the one that strictly follows CONVENTIONS.md line 133. The only caller (line 1608) passes htn positionally and needs adjusting if h₁ is dropped.

The doc at lines 964-967 reads as unconditional, while the statement at line 969 takes h₁ : parent h this ≠ this and h₂ : parent h this ≠ childAt h this s.other. The write order confirms h₂ is needed: setChild thisParent ps top (line 200) is followed by setChild top s this (line 201), so with P = top and ps = s the slot ends holding this. h₁ is needed for the parent-word conjunct, because P = this gets its parent overwritten by top. The hypotheses are visible in the signature, so this is polish rather than dishonesty. The proposed doc addition is accurate.

heap-layer.md lines 155-156 say in the present tense "The theorem also states exactly which addresses' fields changed ... Later frame arguments need that list." That sentence follows the sketch block. The As-built paragraph at lines 143-149 already says the list lives in rotateAt_refines_left_frame/_right_frame, and the statements of rotateAt_refines_left/_right conclude only Located. The sentence is stale plan text that contradicts the As-built paragraph two lines above it. Either fix works; deleting it is simplest.

README.md line 42 does say "`rotate` proven to perform the zipper rotation (the other proofs are the next steps ...)". The trust-base paragraph (lines 140-147) lists five proven functions: rotate, attach_to, substitute_with, switch_with and insert_fixup. The table understates what is proven and contradicts the same file. The proposed row text is correct.

The premise that every caller supplies the witness as hr.root_mem hn is false. Rep.climb calls hl.root_fields hx and hr.root_fields hx at lines 586 and 598, and the disjointness proof calls hl.root_fields hxl and hr.root_fields hxr at lines 655-656. Each of those passes an arbitrary member x of the subtree. There, membership is exactly the information on hand, and a ≠ head is not directly available: it would need a separate lemma (head ∉ t.toList, or root_mem's converse). Taking membership is the more general and more convenient form for those callers. Only line 2188 goes through root_mem, and substituteWith_refines_core's hthis is discharged by `by simp` at its callers. The statement is honest, and the proposed change would make the internal callers worse.

review.summary: I checked every Rust-modelling definition in Heap.lean against rbtree.rs, write by write and read by read, and found no fidelity defect. That covers the accessors, the mutators, initHead, rotateAt, attachTo, substituteWith, switchWith, unlinkFromChain, linkIntoChain, both fix-up loops, the two descents, insertCounted and eraseCountedWith. Fixup.lean's insFix, stage2L/R, delFix, eraseAt, insert and erase, and Arith.lean's models, also match their Rust case for case, and hpha.cpp where they model HPHA. The defects are all in documentation and checking: step numbering that the departure lists cite but the design note never defines, one HPHA-side extra read missing from the module doc's list, a cross-check blind spot on four of link_into_chain's writes, and a few stale or inaccurate doc sentences.

findings.title: "Step 3c" is cited by the departure lists but never defined, and "step 4" means two things in the note
findings.description: CONVENTIONS.md:121, the required departure list, says the fuel of erase_fixup and the descents is "to be proven by the heap layer's steps 3c and 4". Heap.lean:53 says the same ("it is the plan's steps 3c and 4"), and Heap.lean:1558 calls the scratch-parent property "step 3c's hole invariant". docs/heap-layer.md, the plan these refer to, has no 3a/3b/3c: §5 has a single row "3" ("Steps 2–5 of §4 (steps 2 and 3 ✅)"). The note also calls the same hole invariant "the hole invariant of step 4" (heap-layer.md:36-37, meaning §4's theorem 4). Yet at heap-layer.md:132-136, "Left for step 4" and "The step-4 theorems will add head ≠ null" mean the plan's step 4 (§5, the counted operations). The same paragraph says "until then, the step-3 theorems about the Node branch take `!chained h node` as a hypothesis". No step-3 theorem concerns the Node branch: that is §4 item 6, plan step 4. And no theorem in Heap.lean mentions `chained` (grep: only lines 135, 136, 441, 449). A reader following a departure's "settled by step 3c" pointer into the note cannot find it.
findings.evidence: Read the files and grepped for 3a/3b/3c in Lean/docs, README.md, CONVENTIONS.md, Oris/ and CHANGELOG.md. Hits are only in CONVENTIONS.md:121, Heap.lean (17, 24, 53, 1287, 1558, 1699, 1701, 1844) and CHANGELOG.md (15, 20); there are none in heap-layer.md. Grepped `chained` in Heap.lean: no theorem takes it.
findings.fix: In heap-layer.md §5, split row 3 into named sub-steps: 3a = §4 theorem 2 (structural operations), 3b = §4 theorem 3 (insert_fixup), 3c = §4 theorem 4 (erase_fixup and the hole invariant), 3d = §4 theorem 5 (cached root). In §1, write "the hole invariant of step 3c (§4, theorem 4)" instead of "of step 4". In §3, reword to "the step-4 theorems about the `Node` branch will take `!chained h node` as a hypothesis". Keep the convention: "step N" always means a §5 plan step and "§4, theorem N" means a theorem.

findings.title: eraseFixupHpha's extra root read is a departure from hpha.cpp listed only in the definition's doc
findings.description: eraseFixupLoop (Heap.lean:330-331) says: "With `reread`, the root is read before the test's `&&`, where HPHA reads it only when `cur` is black: a read, so no field changes." That is a departure of eraseFixupHpha from `Cpp/hpha.cpp` `erase_fixup` (`while (!cur->red() && cur != mHead.child(LEFT))`). The module doc's list mentions eraseFixupHpha only as "re-reads it, as `Cpp/hpha.cpp` does" (lines 55-57). Its "Not modelled" section lists only reads the model omits, not one it adds. It also calls the fuel "this file's one departure from the Rust's behaviour" (line 48), which is true of the Rust but leaves the HPHA-side departure unlisted. CONVENTIONS.md, "Departures are listed", requires both places.
findings.evidence: Compared eraseFixupLoop (Heap.lean:337-338, `let root := if reread then childAt h head .left else root₀` before `if !red h cur && cur != root`) with hpha.cpp:41. Every other read and write of eraseFixupLoop matches hpha.cpp:41-75 and rbtree.rs:697-774. HPHA's third case reads `w->child(s)` twice where the Rust reads it once, which is value-equivalent because `make_red(w)` changes no link.
findings.fix: Add a bullet to the module doc, for example under "Not modelled" or next to the two readings: "`eraseFixupHpha` reads the root at every loop test before testing `cur`'s colour, where `hpha.cpp` reads it only when `cur` is black (the `&&` short-circuits): an extra read, which changes no field."

findings.title: The cross-check cannot see four of link_into_chain's writes (a chained member's children, side and colour)
findings.description: CONVENTIONS.md:227-229 says the heap model "transcribes [the pointer code] write by write, and the cross-check runs it". The trace prints full records only for tree nodes (write_heap_shape / heapNode). A chained, non-attached member appears only as an id inside its representative's `[next|prev]` lists. So linkIntoChain's writes `setChild this .left null`, `setChild this .right null`, `setParentSide this .left` and `makeRed this` (Heap.lean:271-275) are never compared. They are never read before being overwritten either: only `parent = null` is observed, through `isAttached` choosing Link or Promote, and a later Promote's `switch_with` overwrites children, side and colour. Dropping or changing any of these four writes passes xcheck. The README's injected-fault list (README.md:129-131) tests only the neighbour links. linkIntoChain matches rbtree.rs:592-613 today, but nothing would catch a later regression, and step 4's `Groups` relation will want these fields pinned.
findings.evidence: Read rbtree.rs's write_heap_shape and write_chain (around lines 1884-1945), which print member ids only, and XCheck.lean's heapNode and chain (lines 108-125). Then traced erase_counted's Promote path (rbtree.rs:961-969): switch_with writes this.left, this.right, the parent word's pointer and side, and set_colour, before anything reads them.
findings.fix: Extend the trace format, in both the Rust producer and Tools/XCheck.lean as CONVENTIONS.md:232 requires, to print each non-attached chain member's whole record. For example, write each chain entry as `id:parent:side:colour:left:right`, or add a fourth `|` section listing every live non-attached node's record. Then add a README fault injection such as "a chain member left black".

findings.title: insFix's doc assigns the no-parent exit to the last arm; the first arm handles it
findings.description: insFix's doc says: "The last arm is the loop's exit with `p` black (or no parent at all: `cur` is the root), plus the unreachable red-root shape". The no-parent case is the first arm, `| .root, t => (t.setBlack, 0)` (line 123), which matches before the last arm, so the last arm never sees `.root`. Rule 2 asks each arm's doc to say which Rust case it is.
findings.evidence: Read insFix (Fixup.lean:122-144). Arm order makes `.root` unreachable in the catch-all arm.
findings.fix: "The first arm is the exit at the root (`cur` has no parent: `p` is the black sentinel); the last arm is the exit with `p` black, plus the unreachable red-root shape discussed in the module doc."

findings.title: Arith.lean says "Departures: none" but does not say that the Rust's debug_assert!s are not modelled
findings.description: The module doc says "**Departures from the Rust: none.**" Four Rust functions it models carry debug_assert!s that panic in debug builds: `round_up` (`align.is_power_of_two()`), `bucket_spacing_function` (`size > 0 && size <= MAX_SMALL_ALLOCATION`), `_aligned` (also `size % MIN_ALLOCATION == 0`) and `_inverse` (`index < NUM_BUCKETS`). Heap.lean lists its debug_assert!s under "Not modelled"; Arith.lean is silent. As a result, bucketSpacingAligned_eq's doc remark "(at `0` both wrap to `usize::MAX`)" (line 352-353) describes the release build only: in a debug build both functions panic on their assertion at 0. Similarly, small_alloc_bucket's doc (line 400-402) says `alloc` sends every small request to a bucket, but `orisnik.rs` `alloc` returns `None` for `size == 0` first. The theorem is merely stronger there, not wrong.
findings.evidence: Read align.rs:19-22, bucket.rs:95-112 and orisnik.rs:476-485, and compared with Arith.lean's docs.
findings.fix: Add a "Not modelled" sentence: "The Rust's `debug_assert!`s (`round_up`'s power-of-two alignment; the bucket functions' range checks), which the theorems' hypotheses satisfy wherever they matter." Qualify line 353 as "(in a release build; a debug build's assertion rejects 0)" and mention `alloc`'s `size == 0` early return in small_alloc_bucket's doc.

recommendations: I confirmed these by side-by-side reading, so they need no fix. rotateAt reads ps, then thisParent, top and topSChild, then makes the nine writes, as in rbtree.rs:364-394. attachTo reads leafChild after the two neighbour writes. switchWith reads node's parent after the two set_child writes and node's colour after all the writes. substituteWith reads parent_side before parent. insertFixupLoop, both branches and the inner rotation, matches rbtree.rs:623-677. eraseFixupLoop, all four cases including w re-read after make_red(p), matches 697-774. The descents and eraseCountedWith's branch structure, red(repl) read before child(repl, s), match 892-1013. initHead matches head_ptr's first-touch writes. The NodeRec defaults match NodeBase::UNLINKED / TaggedPtr::null.

In Fixup.lean I checked insFix's four arms (inner rotate(p, s) with s = p's side), stage2L/R's third case (rotate(w, o) brings w.child(s) up) and fourth case, and delFix's case-1 path (p painted red, sibling w.child(s), stage2 called with pc = red). eraseAt's three Rust branches, including repl being the right child itself, match rbtree.rs and hpha.cpp. Every departure in its module list also appears in the definition docs.

Arith.lean: normalizeSize, MAX_ALLOCATION, growSize, the bucket functions, clampSmall (saturating_add and wrapping_sub) and isSmall match tree.rs, bucket.rs and align.rs operator for operator. hphaRoundUp matches hpha.h:117 `(x + (a-1)) & -(int)a`.

Optional hardening for xcheck: the trace never prints head.right, head.prev or head.next. No valid-tree path writes them today, since every root write uses side Left. Printing them in the sentinel section would turn a stray write into a mismatch for free.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified. heap-layer.md has no 3a/3b/3c anywhere. Its §5 row 3 is "Steps 2–5 of §4 (steps 2 and 3 ✅)", so the note itself numbers §4's items as "steps". That makes "step N" ambiguous within the note. Line 37 ("the hole invariant of step 4") and line 166 ("step 4's hole invariant") mean §4 item 4, erase_fixup, which is part of plan step 3. Lines 132-137 ("Left for step 4", "The step-4 theorems will add head ≠ null") mean §5 plan step 4. Line 137 ("the step-3 theorems about the `Node` branch take `!chained h node`") points to theorems that belong to §4 item 6, i.e. plan step 4. Grep confirms that no theorem in Heap.lean mentions `chained` (only lines 135, 136, 441, 449). review.summary: The Heap.lean proofs are sound and fast: the whole module elaborates in about 3.1 s (`lake env lean Oris/RB/Heap.lean`), so performance is not a problem. Their weakness is how they are written. A lot is repeated: the two rotations, the eight cases of `insertFixupLoop_refines`, and a sentinel-or-member case split that appears 27 times. Several proofs also depend on the exact shape of definitions or library lemmas: `insertFixupLoop` is unfolded by hand eight times, there are positional `.2.2.2.2.2.1` projections into `node_inv` and into the raw `List.nodup_append` normal form, a `simp [*]`, and `rfl` steps that unfold `insFix`. I compiled the most valuable factorings in scratch files against the built project: loop step lemmas, `Rep.ne_root`, a `reroot` proof through `nodup_node`, and `insFix` without `rfl`. All of them work, and they carry over directly to step 3c, where `delFix` is well-founded and `rfl` cannot unfold it (I checked this).

findings.title: insertFixupLoop is unfolded by hand in all eight cases; per-branch step lemmas would remove this
findings.description: Each of the eight non-exit cases of `insertFixupLoop_refines` ends by unfolding the loop's definition with a long `simp only`. Red-uncle cases (lines 1962-1963, 2021-2022, 2079-2080, 2145-2146): `simp only [insertFixupLoop, red, hyr, parent, parentSide, hyz, hys, Side.other, childAt, huv, hcol, makeBlack, makeRed, setColour_parent, colourBit, ite_true]`. Black-uncle cases (1985-1988, 2044-2047, 2110-2113, 2176-2179): `rw [insertFixupLoop]; simp only [red, hyr, ..., Bool.false_eq_true, ite_true, ite_false, hcy, makeBlack, makeRed]`. These blocks depend on simp normalising the `let (h, cur, p, rotations) := if … then … else …` tuple destructuring in the definition, and on the names `ite_true`, `ite_false` and `Bool.false_eq_true`. This is the part of the file most likely to break on a toolchain bump or a small change to `insertFixupLoop`, and it breaks in eight places at once. `eraseFixupLoop` (step 3c) has two such tuple-`let`s and four cases, so repeating the pattern there would make it worse.
findings.evidence: Scratch file `robust1.lean`: the three lemmas below compile against the built project. Scratch file `robust2.lean`: a copy of `insertFixupLoop_refines` whose four red-uncle endings are replaced by `rw [← hH, insertFixupLoop_red_uncle hyr hyz hys (by simpa only [red, childAt, Side.other, huv] using hcol)]; simp only [makeRed, makeBlack, childAt, Side.other, huv, colourBit, parent, setColour_parent]` compiles with no error.
findings.fix:
Add one unfolding lemma per loop branch, each stated once and side-generic (the loop is already side-generic):
```lean
theorem insertFixupLoop_red_uncle {head fuel h cur p pp s rot} (hp : red h p = true)
    (hpp : parent h p = pp) (hs : parentSide h p = s) (hu : red h (childAt h pp s.other) = true) :
    insertFixupLoop head (fuel + 1) h cur p rot =
      insertFixupLoop head fuel (makeRed (makeBlack (makeBlack h p) (childAt h pp s.other)) pp)
        pp (parent h pp) rot := by
  rw [insertFixupLoop]; subst hpp hs
  simp only [hp, hu, ite_true]; simp only [makeRed, makeBlack, parent, setColour_parent]

theorem insertFixupLoop_black_uncle_outer … (hu : red h (childAt h pp s.other) = false)
    (hc : cur ≠ childAt h p s.other) :
    insertFixupLoop head (fuel + 1) h cur p rot =
      insertFixupLoop head fuel (rotateAt (makeRed (makeBlack h p) pp) pp s.other) cur p (rot + 1)

theorem insertFixupLoop_black_uncle_inner … (hc : cur = childAt h p s.other) :
    insertFixupLoop head (fuel + 1) h cur p rot =
      insertFixupLoop head fuel
        (rotateAt (makeRed (makeBlack (rotateAt h p s) (parent (rotateAt h p s) p)) pp) pp s.other)
        p (parent (rotateAt h p s) p) (rot + 2)
```
Each is proved by `rw [insertFixupLoop]; simp only [hp, hpp, hs, hu, hc, ite_true, ite_false, Bool.false_eq_true]`, and they sit next to `insertFixupLoop_exit`. Before writing 3c, add the matching set for `eraseFixupLoop`: `eraseFixupLoop_exit`, `_case1` (w red), `_case2`, and `_case34` (with and without case 3), stated with `parent h cur = p` and `parentSide h cur = s` as hypotheses. The refinement proof then never unfolds the loop.

findings.fix:
Add next to `Rep.root_mem`:
```lean
theorem Rep.ne_root (hr : Rep h head k q σ u) (hxh : x ≠ head) (hxu : x ∉ u.toList) : x ≠ k :=
  fun e => by
    by_cases hk : k = head
    · exact hxh (e.trans hk)
    · exact hxu (e ▸ hr.root_mem hk)

theorem Rep.ne_root_of_mem (hr : Rep h head k q σ u) (hv : Rep h head a p' σ' v)
```

findings.title: switchWith_apply closes its goals with `simp [*]`, partly non-terminal (`simp [*]; cases ps <;> rfl`)
findings.description: Lines 1519-1534 close every branch with `simp [*]`, and three of them use it non-terminally: `subst e₃; subst e₅; simp [*]; cases ps <;> rfl` (1523), `subst e₃; simp [*]; cases ps <;> rfl` (1524), `subst e₄; simp [*]; cases ps <;> rfl` (1530). `simp [*]` hands simp every hypothesis in context, including the generalisation equations `hL`, `hR`, `hP`, `hps` and `hc`. Which of them each branch actually uses is invisible. Adding a hypothesis, or a change in how simp orients one, changes the outcome. The sibling proofs `rotateAt_apply` and `substituteWith_apply` give explicit lemma lists. The proof also relies on `subst e₁` (`e₁ : x = this`) eliminating `this` rather than `x`.
findings.evidence: In scratch file `sw.lean` I replaced each `simp [*]` with what looked like the needed list (e.g. `simp [hP, hc, h₂, h₃, hn5, hn6, hn7]` after `subst e₁`). Two branches still failed: an unsolved `if x = P …` goal and a failing `cases ps <;> rfl`. So the proof needs more of the context than it appears to, and nobody reading it can know which parts.
findings.fix: Rewrite the proof in the style of `rotateAt_apply`. Generalise only what the statement mentions, finish the `simp only [switchWith, …]` prelude with the generalisation equations included, so that no `(h node).…` term is left for `[*]` to catch, then do the case split and close each branch with an explicit `simp [e…, hn…]`. Do the `cases ps` before the closing `simp`, so that no `simp` is non-terminal.

findings.title: `rfl` steps unfold insFix by definitional reduction; the same style cannot work for the well-founded delFix
findings.description: Four times, `have hz : insFix (.left .red (.left c' gp z (.node .red ul uv ur)) y b) t = insFix gp (…) := by rfl` (1956-1958, 2015-2017, 2073-2075, 2139-2141), plus `rw [insFix, ite_eq_right hu]; rfl` (2104, 2170) and the closing `rfl`s at 1913, 1988, 2047, 2113 and 2179. These rely on `insFix` being compiled by structural recursion, so the kernel can unfold it and decide `red? (node red …)`. `delFix` is defined with `termination_by path` (Fixup.lean:449), and `rfl` does not unfold it. Copying the 3b proof style into 3c will therefore fail, and the two proofs will end up in different styles.
findings.evidence: Scratch file `robust1.lean`: `simp only [insFix, red?, ite_true, RBNode.setBlack]` closes the `hz` of line 1956 without `rfl`. Scratch file `wf.lean`: `delFix (.left .black pp y .nil) (.node .red x 1 .nil) = (… .fill …, 0) := by rfl` fails ('not definitionally equal'), while `rw [delFix]; rfl` succeeds. Fixup.lean already uses `rw [delFix.eq_def]` (lines 474, 815, 833, …).
findings.fix: Use the equation lemmas consistently: `rw [insFix]` / `simp only [insFix, red?, ite_true, RBNode.setBlack]` in place of the bare `rfl`s. Before 3c, add per-arm equation lemmas for `delFix` in Fixup.lean, next to `delFix_red`, e.g. `delFix_left_red_sibling (hx : red? x = false) : delFix (.left pc pp y (node red wl wv wr)) x = match stage2L … with …`. The heap proof can then rewrite with named facts instead of `delFix.eq_def` plus a `simp only` that depends on the `match` compilation.

findings.title: Non-terminal bare `simp` followed by `cases … <;> rfl`
findings.description: `substituteWith_apply` line 1376: `· subst e₂; simp; cases ps <;> rfl`, a bare non-terminal `simp`. `rotateAt_apply` lines 1018-1019 (`subst e₂; simp [e₁, h₃, h₅]` then `cases s <;> rfl`) and 1023-1024 (`simp [e₁, e₂]` then `cases s <;> cases ps <;> rfl`) are the same pattern with a lemma list. Whatever simp leaves behind must then be closed by `rfl` after the case split, so a change to the simp set (new simp lemmas about structure updates or `if`) changes the residual goal and breaks the `rfl`.
findings.evidence: Reading. Each residual goal is a `NodeRec` structure-update equality that `rfl` closes only in the exact form the current simp leaves.
findings.fix: Split first and finish with simp: `· subst e₂; cases ps <;> simp [NodeRec.withChild]` (and likewise `cases s <;> simp [e₁, h₃, h₅, NodeRec.withChild]`), or replace the bare `simp` with a `simp only [...]` list.

findings.title: Unused lemmas, one with the file's heaviest automation

findings.title: Fixup.lean: `rename_i` with eleven auto-generated names after `split`
findings.description: In the erase spec, `unfold eraseAt; split` is followed by `rename_i c₁ cl ll lv lr x₁ cr rl rv rr hm` (1072), `rename_i c₁ x₁ cr rl rv rr hm` (1069) and `rename_i c₁ l₁ x₁ hm` (1066), and the same again at 1112-1127. The names are bound by the positions of `split`'s inaccessible hypotheses, which depend on how `eraseAt`'s `match` is compiled and on `split`'s implementation. If either changes, the names land on the wrong variables, with confusing errors. The `fun_induction` proofs in the same file avoid `caseN` names for this reason (comment at 516-518), but these sites were not changed in the same way.
findings.evidence: Reading (`grep rename_i`: 39 occurrences in Fixup.lean; the ones binding more than two names are at 835-923 and 1065-1127).
findings.fix: Do the case split on the explicit shape instead of `split`: `match hm : r, l with …`, or `rcases` on a small lemma `eraseAt_cases` that states the three shapes with named components. Or at least add a comment, as at 516-518, saying which constructor's fields each `rename_i` binds.

recommendations: Do these in order of payoff, before 3c: R1 (loop step lemmas; also write the `eraseFixupLoop_case*` versions first), R3 (`Rep.ne_root`), R4/R5 (named projections, a single home for the `List.nodup_append` shape), then R2 (side-generic `rotateAt_refines` via `nodeOn`). Together they should cut `insertFixupLoop_refines` and the rotation proofs by roughly a third. More importantly, 3c's proof can then be written mostly as one side-generic argument rather than mirrored pairs.

Add a short 'Proof robustness' section to CONVENTIONS.md: no `simp [*]`, no non-terminal bare `simp`/`simp_all`, no `rfl` that unfolds a recursive definition (use its equation lemmas), named fields rather than `.2.2.2` projections into conjunctions of more than three facts, and `rename_i` only with a comment saying what it binds. `Tools/Audit.lean`'s banned-construct lint could flag `simp [*]` and `simp_all [*]` cheaply.
Elaboration time is not a concern: `time lake env lean Oris/RB/Heap.lean` reports 3.1 s for the whole module, so the factorings above are for robustness, not speed.

When Heap.lean is split, put the per-branch loop lemmas (R1) and `insertFixupLoop_exit` in the fix-ups file next to the refinement theorems, and `Rep.ne_root`, `nodup_node` and the named-field views in the relation file, so that 3c imports them without the structural-operation proofs.

'Most likely part of the file to break' is a judgment call, but the fix is correct and has been tested.

The duplication is real. A diff of Heap.lean 1112-1129 against 1242-1259 shows the HH block differs only in the side argument on its first three lines, and `rotateAt_refines_left` and `_right` mirror each other. However, CONVENTIONS.md 172-174 makes mirror-image definitions (`L`/`R`) and mirror-image theorems (`_left`/`_right`) a naming convention, and Fixup.lean is written in that style throughout, so side-specific pairs are an accepted pattern, not a defect. The full `nodeOn` generalisation is a large refactor whose payoff for 3c is a guess. It changes how the Located/Rep lemmas are stated, and nobody has tested it (the `rotate`/`nodeOn` rfl identity does hold by hand-checking). The cheap, clearly worthwhile part is lifting the duplicated HH sentinel block into one side-generic lemma, in the style of `substituteWith_refines_core`.

verdicts.reasoning: `grep -c 'by_cases h[a-zA-Z]*h : [a-zA-Z]* = head'` gives 27 in Heap.lean. There are positional projections such as `Ly.1.node_inv.2.2.2.2.2.1` (Heap.lean 1993, and the other listed lines) for the colour conjunct of the eight-way `Rep.node_inv`. Readers do have to count through the statement, and adding a conjunct would shift every index. It is a readability and maintenance cost, not a correctness or honesty issue, hence low rather than medium. The fix is sound: anonymous-constructor `obtain ⟨…⟩` works on structures, and `Located.root_red` alone covers the most frequent read.

`Rep.reroot` (Heap.lean 700-710) projects `hnd.2.2 …` and `hnd.2.1.1` out of the `List.nodup_append`/`nodup_cons` normal form, and `Located.outside` (822-832) does the same with `hnd.1.2.2`/`hnd.2.2`. `nodup_node` (803) depends only on `RBNode.toList_node` and sits after `namespace Rep`, so it can move up. Real: `switchWith_apply` (Heap.lean 1519-1534) closes branches with `simp [*]`, three of them non-terminally (`simp [*]; cases ps <;> rfl`). But the reviewer's attempt to replace `[*]` with explicit lists failed (sw.lean), so the proposed rewrite is unvalidated and the hardest part. I tested a smaller fix in scratch: `cases ps <;> simp [*, NodeRec.withChild]` in place of each `simp [*]; cases ps <;> rfl`. It compiles, and it removes the non-terminal simp, the more fragile half. The `subst e₁` concern is spurious: whichever variable `subst` eliminates, the remaining goal is the same up to renaming, and `simp [*]` closes it. Severity is low: the lemma is a local apply lemma with a precise statement, so if it breaks it breaks visibly.

Replacing `[*]` with explicit lists is optional polish, and it needs the generalisation equations named.

verdicts.reasoning: True that `rfl` cannot unfold the well-founded `delFix` (Fixup.lean 425-450, `termination_by path`). But the 3b `rfl`s on the structurally recursive `insFix` are sound and stable: the kernel reliably unfolds structural recursion, so they are not a robustness defect. The reviewer's own evidence is partly wrong. In wf.lean, the claimed-working `rw [delFix]; rfl` also fails ('unsolved goals case x_1 … nil = node red … → False'), and the example has a red `x`, so it exercises only the first `if` branch. In scratch I tested the proposed reordering: `subst e₂; cases ps <;> simp [NodeRec.withChild]` in `substituteWith_apply`, and `cases s <;> cases ps <;> simp [NodeRec.withChild]` in `rotateAt_apply`. Both compile. The fix needs `NodeRec.withChild` in the simp set, as the reviewer wrote. A plain `simp` after the split leaves `withChild` goals unsolved. But heap-layer.md lists them explicitly as step-1 deliverables (the frame part of `rotate`), so they are documented API, not dead code. `rotateAt_links` (955-962) does not use `simp_all`: it is already `simp only` plus `by_cases` plus a terminal `simp`, so that part of the finding is wrong. Only `rotateAt_parent_fields` (968-986) uses `simp_all`, and it is terminal in every branch. Keeping documented API is a judgment call. Deferring the review until 3c, as the reviewer also suggests, is reasonable.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Optionally re-prove `rotateAt_parent_fields` without `simp_all`, possibly from `rotateAt_apply`. At 3c, delete any frame lemma that is still unused and update heap-layer.md §step 1 to match.

verdicts.reasoning: Fixup.lean 1065-1072 and 1112-1127 use `unfold eraseAt; split` followed by `rename_i` with up to 11 positional names (`rename_i c₁ cl ll lv lr x₁ cr rl rv rr hm`). These names depend on `split`'s generated inaccessible hypotheses. This is a common Lean idiom, and the subsequent `cases hm` would fail loudly rather than silently, but it is the same kind of fragility the file's own comment at 516-518 avoids for `fun_induction`. review.summary: The docs mostly agree with the code. Every citable Heap.lean declaration has a doc comment, and the README, CONVENTIONS and design-note claims about 3a/3b match the theorem statements. The real problems are four. The README's layout row for Heap.lean is stale, and the README lists the proven heap theorems under "What is not (yet) proven". The 3a/3b/3c step labels are used everywhere but defined nowhere, and they clash with §4's own numbering. Three docs give the wrong reason why Oris.lean must import every module. heap-layer.md describes `!chained` hypotheses that no theorem has. Heap.lean (2,228 lines) splits cleanly into a model, a relation, a heap-algebra file and two refinement files, with no renames; the audit and the lakefile need no code change, but Oris.lean must import each new module directly.

findings.title: Oris.lean, CONVENTIONS and the audit give the wrong reason why Oris.lean must import every module
findings.description: Oris.lean says "`lake build` builds what is imported here". CONVENTIONS.md:81-82 says "`lake build` builds what `Oris.lean` imports, so the audit also fails if `Oris.lean` does not import a module". Tools/Audit.lean:18 says "since `lake build` builds what `Oris.lean` imports", and its failure message (line 178) says "so `lake build` does not build it". README.md:43 says "(what `lake build` builds)". But lakefile.toml declares `globs = ["Oris.*"]`. In Lake, `X.*` is `Glob.andSubmodules`: X plus every module found on disk below it. So `lake build` builds every file under Oris/ whether Oris.lean imports it or not. The import check still matters, for another reason: `lake env leanchecker --fresh Oris` replays module `Oris` and its imports, so a module that Oris.lean misses would escape the kernel replay. This matters for the split (S5), which adds modules.
findings.evidence: Lake source for the pinned toolchain: Lake/Load/Toml.lean:103 maps a trailing '*' to `.andSubmodules`. Lake/Config/Glob.lean:24-25 and 58-59: andSubmodules = "the specified module and all submodules", enumerated with forEachModuleInDir. lakefile.toml:12-13 has `globs = ["Oris.*"]`.
findings.fix: Oris.lean: "-- Every proof module. `lake env leanchecker --fresh Oris` replays what is imported here, and `lake exe audit` (Tools/Audit.lean) fails if a module under `Oris/` is missing from this list." review.summary: The relation is ready for 3c and needs no change. `Located` already handles an empty hole, because the occupant is an index and is never read. The hole invariant fits as one extra conjunct, `parent h cur = P ∧ parentSide h cur = S`. `substituteWith_refines_*` and `switchWith_refines` already produce that conjunct, and the up/down/paint/rotate lemmas cover every move `erase_fixup` makes. The real gaps are elsewhere. 3c cannot take insert's "every located input" form: on a tree whose sibling is the sentinel (a red-black tree never has one), the heap model ends with the sentinel red while `delFix` does not, so the theorem needs a no-departure hypothesis. The Rust's once-read root needs a black-root hypothesis, which §6 and `Fixup.lean` leave out. Three docs misstate things: `heap-layer.md` §4 step 4, the cross-check's "root changed" coverage item, and the audit lint, which `#eval!` and `_root_.Lean.` get past (both confirmed).

findings.title: 3c cannot be stated for every located input: at a sentinel sibling the heap model turns the sentinel red
findings.description: `insertFixupLoop_refines` holds for every located input with a black root, and nothing in the plan says `erase_fixup` will be different. It will be. `Fixup.lean` has a departure at a nil sibling (`stage2L`/`stage2R`, Fixup.lean 367-372: "A `nil` sibling is unreachable ... the model returns `none` there"). In the heap model, which follows the Rust, that state goes further: `w` is the sentinel, `childAt h head .left` is the root, and when the root is black, case 2 runs `make_red(w)`, which paints the sentinel red. `RepPath.root` and `Tree` both require `(h head).red = false`. So `eraseFixupLoop_refines` is false without a hypothesis that rules out this departure. That hypothesis is a balance or no-nil-sibling condition carried through every iteration and after case 1. §4 step 4 never says this, and the only `hpha_*` lemma it cites, it cites for the wrong reason (see D2).
findings.evidence: Scratch file audit/nilsib.lean. The heap is head=1 (black), root 2 (black, left child 3, right child the sentinel), cur=3 (black). `eraseFixup 10 h0 1 3` and `eraseFixupHpha` both return `(h 1).red = true`. `delFix (.left .black .root 2 .nil) (.node .black .nil 3 .nil)` returns a tree, and the sentinel's colour is not part of it.
findings.fix: Decide the hypothesis's form before writing 3c, and record the decision in §4 step 4. The best option: in Fixup.lean, define a predicate `DelFixClean : Path α → RBNode α → Prop` by the same recursion as `delFix`, true when `delFix` never reaches the nil-sibling arm (the sibling of a black non-root `cur` is non-nil, and after case 1 so is the red sibling's near child, recursively on the case-2 branch). Prove `delFixClean_of_balanced` from the invariant of `delFix_balanced_aux`. That proof reuses `hpha_sibling_not_sentinel_*` and `hpha_sibling_after_case1_not_sentinel_*`, ideally by extracting the per-case propagation steps out of `delFix_balanced_aux` first. The heap theorem then takes `DelFixClean path x`, which keeps black heights out of Heap.lean. It holds for every input on which the zipper model takes no departure, and the spec theorem supplies the hypothesis from `Path.Balanced`.

findings.evidence: Reading the code. In a `Node` erase, the root's address changes when the erased node is the root (the sentinel's link is rewritten by `substituteWith` or `switchWith`) or when a fix-up rotates at the root. The condition does not separate the two.

findings.title: §4 step 4's case for the hole invariant leans on a lemma it does not need, and misses a lemma it does
findings.description: "The proof shows the scratch is read only in the first iteration, and that no write reaches it before that read. Case 1's rotation would clobber it only if `w.child(s)` were the sentinel, which `hpha_sibling_after_case1_not_sentinel_*` rules out." `eraseFixupLoop` reads `p := parent h cur` and `s := parentSide h cur` at the very top of the iteration (Heap.lean 339-340), before any write, and later reads use those locals. From the second iteration on, `cur` is a real node: case 2 sets `cur := p`, which is a path node and so not the sentinel, and case 4 ends the loop. A write to the scratch fields by case 1 or case 4 therefore never matters, and the hole invariant needs no balance hypothesis at all. The passage also misses the loop's other dependence on the sentinel's fields: the loop test `cur != root` needs the root's address, which is a path address whenever the path is non-empty (`RepPath.root_mem` below).
findings.evidence: Reading `eraseFixupLoop` (Heap.lean 336-382): the only reads of `cur`'s `parent` word are the two `let`s right after the test.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence: the scratch is read only at the top of the first iteration, before any write, and every later iteration starts from a real node, so writes to it (case 1's or case 4's rotation when `top_s_child` is the sentinel) are irrelevant. Then point to R1 for the reason 3c still needs a balance-derived hypothesis.

recommendations: The 3c loop theorem, sketched, with one theorem covering both root readings: `theorem eraseFixupLoop_refines (head : Addr) (reread : Bool) (root₀ : Addr) : ∀ (fuel : Nat) {h : Heap} {cur P : Addr} {S : Side} {x : RBNode Addr} {path : Path Addr} (rot : Nat), Located h head cur P S x path → parent h cur = P → parentSide h cur = S → (reread = false → childAt h head .left = root₀) → (reread = false → rootColour path ≠ some .red) → DelFixClean path x → pathDepth path + 1 ≤ fuel → ∃ H, eraseFixupLoop head reread root₀ fuel h cur rot = some (H, rot + (delFix path x).2) ∧ Tree H head (delFix path x).1`. Two of the hypotheses come for free. The hole conjunct is automatic for a real `cur` (`Rep.root_fields`), and `substituteWith_refines_*` and `switchWith_refines` already produce it at entry. The `root₀` hypothesis is only needed at recursive calls after a case 2 without a case 1, where the root is unchanged. Keep the hole invariant out of `Located`, so every existing lemma stays as it is: no change to the relation is needed.

Three helper lemmas, written and type-checked in scratch (audit/proto.lean). `theorem setColour_of_eq {h a b} (e : (h a).red = b) : setColour h a b = h`, needed for the final `make_black` on the sentinel and for the §6 "already black" writes. `theorem Located.makeBlack_fill (hl : Located h head a p s t path) : Tree (makeBlack h a) head (path.fill t.setBlack)`, which generalises `Tree.makeBlack_root` and covers both of `delFix`'s exits (a red `cur`, and the `.root` arm, the sentinel included). `theorem RepPath.root_mem (hp : RepPath h head a p s path) : path = .root ∧ childAt h head .left = a ∨ childAt h head .left ∈ path.listL ++ path.listR`, which together with `Located.outside` decides the loop test `cur != root`.

Before 3c, add side-generic forms so each erase case is proven once rather than once per side. `insertFixupLoop_refines` has eight near-duplicate cases; `delFix` would need about twelve leaves per side. Written and type-checked in scratch (audit/side.lean): `def nodeOn : Side → RBColor → RBNode Addr → Addr → RBNode Addr → RBNode Addr` (the near child on side s), `def stepOn : Side → RBColor → Path Addr → Addr → RBNode Addr → Path Addr`, `theorem rotateAt_refines (s) (hl : Located h head a p σ (nodeOn s c l a (nodeOn s c' rl b rr)) path) : Located (rotateAt h a s) head b p σ (nodeOn s c' (nodeOn s c l a rl) b rr) path`, `Located.up s` and `Located.down s` (the latter landing at `childAt h y s`). Each is a two-line `cases s`. Matching `stage2L`/`stage2R` then becomes one `cases s` at the zipper equation.

Fuel: `pathDepth path + 1 ≤ fuel` carries over from insert, with one trap. After case 1 then case 2, the zipper recurses on `.left black pp wv wr`, which has the same depth as before. So that branch must close with an exit lemma (`cur = p` is red, as in `delFix_red`), not with the induction hypothesis. Provide equation lemmas in the style of `insertFixupLoop_exit` (`eraseFixupLoop_exit_red`, `eraseFixupLoop_exit_root`) so the tuple-`let`s are unfolded in only one place. For a depth-based fuel theorem with an empty hole, `(path.fill .nil).depth` can equal `pathDepth path`, so the `+1` comes from the non-nil sibling (DelFixClean) or from the pre-erase tree.

Step-4 preparation that 3c's entry point depends on. `switchWith_refines` describes only the subtree rooted at `node`. When the successor `repl` is deeper than `node`'s right child, the hole is inside that subtree, so two more things are needed: (a) a conclusion that `switchWith` keeps the sentinel's `parent` word when the sentinel is neither of `node`'s children (derivable from `switchWith_apply`; when `node` is the root only the sentinel's link is written); and (b) a way to move a deep `Located` through the switch, with `node` replaced by `repl` on the path. This is cheapest as an Oris-side path concatenation (`Path.glue seg path` with `(glue seg path).fill t = path.fill (seg.fill t)`, and `(leftmost t q).2 = glue (leftmost t .root).2 q`), plus `Located.glue` for descending. Both are new lemmas; the relation itself needs no change.

Cross-check coverage for 3c. Count, and require, three cases: erases whose fix-up starts from an empty hole (black `repl` and `replChild = head`); the case where `switch_with` overwrites the scratch fields (`repl = node.right` and `repl.right = head`); and §6's case 1 at the root followed by case 4. All three can be computed in `replay` from the pre-state with the existing `Heap` functions. Also add an executable check of the hole invariant at fix-up entry: replay `substituteWith`/`switchWith` and require `childAt H (H head).parent (H head).side = head` whenever `replChild = head`. That tests the 3c invariant on all 9,935 erases before any proof is written.

Minor cross-check gap: `headInfo` prints the sentinel's `parent` word and colour but not its right link, which `Tree` requires to equal `head`. The step-3a proofs now cover that link for `attach`/`substitute`/`switch`, so this matters little; note it in the README's list of what the comparison covers.
